rationale: This is essentially the archived "Collected-Sales Value" (sales yield × receivables-change) with inventory added and a sign flip, and the nonnegative-rank × signed-z construction parks all expensive firms near zero so the spread is really just a within-cheap working-capital accrual sort (Sloan) rather than a new mechanism.

The payables-stretching haircut on cash-flow yield is a coherent, correctly-signed and relatively under-tested quality-within-value mechanism, though the rank × signed-z form leaves expensive firms clustered near zero and the ingredient overlaps the liability side of the accrual anomaly.

Penalizing EBITDA/EV by depreciation intensity is mechanically close to simply using EBIT/EV, a standard published enterprise multiple, so the signal is more a rediscovery of a known value-measure refinement (plus a capital-intensity/asset-age proxy) than a genuine cross-theme interaction.

(ib − Δwcap)/mktcap is a cash-earnings-to-price measure that both rediscovers the classic accruals-plus-value composite and is a near-cosmetic variant of the archived "Accrual-Stripped Enterprise Yield" and "Working-Capital-Ex Book Value" constructions.

The absolute-value haircut is internally incoherent with the hypothesis—working-capital releases (a cash inflow) are penalized exactly like build-ups—and since che sits inside wcap the term partly penalizes firms for cash growth, leaving little beyond a noisier cash-to-price signal.

This is largely a min-composite of two known yields (dividend yield and cash-flow yield) in the same weakest-link form that already failed in the archive, with an arbitrary sign-blind |aoloch| haircut and a large mass of zero-dividend firms pinned at the bottom rank.
